## Current Code Workflow (from code analyzer)
# Model Overview (for Diagnosis)

The supplied module diagnoses one fitted HSTU model per category. It accesses effective item embeddings through `item_emb`, causal sequence features through `log2feats(sequence)`, and aligned or candidate scores through `predict_score(features, items)`. Inputs contain item IDs and learned absolute positions. For left-padded histories, the final representation comes from the greatest nonpadding index, never `count-1`. Backbone implementation details are not supplied.

# Diagnosis Inputs & Hooks

`DiagnosisProbe(view, device)` receives the host ModelView; `view.model` is the actual network. It reads catalog size, maximum sequence length, category identity, and `user_train['History']`. Loader batches provide `(None, sequence, positive, negative)` with matching B × L tensors; shapes and item IDs are validated.

`run_full_diagnosis` caches at most ten batches, enables evaluation/inference mode, and restores module modes and captured random-generator states afterward.

# Probes & Metrics

- **Embedding collapse:** Samples up to 2,048 item embeddings and rescales their mean off-diagonal cosine to [0,1]. Approximately 0.5 means zero mean cosine; values near 1 indicate strong angular alignment. This does not measure representation rank or recommendation diversity.
- **Positive–negative margins:** Reports mean margin, tenth percentile, negative-wins rate, and fraction below 0.5 over valid training positions. Larger margins and fewer ranking errors generally indicate stronger sampled-pair separation; the threshold depends on score scale.
- **History audit:** Reports original rank, reciprocal rank, and hit@10, plus paired intervention effects. Lower rank and higher reciprocal rank/hit@10 indicate better target placement.
- **Cost:** Records wall time, CUDA interval, peak allocation, and scoring counts.

# Perturbation & Tests

Up to 32 training users contribute two prefixes each; loader rows provide a fallback. Each prefix shares one target and up to 999 unique negatives across variants. Tests remove recent, oldest, final, or prefinal events, and average three nonfinal shuffles. Deletions compact histories and restore left padding. Effects measure frozen-model sensitivity; user-cluster bootstrapping supplies conditional intervals when identities permit.

TREC’s 2025 Product Recommendation task defines substitutes by shared function and complements by related functionality. Its 2026 report distinguishes these relations from compatibility and user preference: a phone case can complement phones generally while fitting only specific models; substitutes may help during selection but be redundant after purchase. Assessors could mark pairs “unable-to-assess,” supporting explicit uncertainty rather than forced labels. Interaction histories alone do not establish ownership, purchase intent, or satisfied needs. [TREC task definitions](https://trec-product-search.github.io/recommendations.html), [2025 track report](https://arxiv.org/html/2608.17138v1).

“Function-based labels for complementary recommendation” warns that co-purchase/co-view labels contain behavioral noise and that binary LLM judgments miss relational nuance. A practical diagnostic adaptation: annotate title/description pairs as substitute, complement, unrelated, or insufficient evidence; record supporting text, functional overlap, and any explicitly stated compatibility constraints. Keep identity uncertainty separate from relation uncertainty. Call recommendations “potentially redundant” rather than asserting unnecessary replacement; treat compatibility and satisfied needs as hypotheses unless observed evidence supports them. [Function-based annotation study](https://www.sciencedirect.com/science/article/pii/S0167865525003976).

Manually double-annotate a category-balanced calibration sample, adjudicate disagreements, and measure per-relation precision, annotator agreement, abstention coverage, and error among accepted labels. Calibrate acceptance thresholds against human judgments rather than trusting verbal confidence. Abstention research supports evaluating the error–coverage tradeoff; it does not establish product-specific reliability without local calibration. Report these probes alongside the fixed macro validation HR@10, without replacing benchmark selection or importing external datasets. [Abstention survey, 2025](https://aclanthology.org/2025.tacl-1.26/).

Practical implication: retain the pinned evaluator for selection, but separately stress-test validation conclusions across candidate sizes, repeated candidate draws, uniform versus popularity sampling, and full-catalog ranking where affordable. Full-catalog evaluation still cannot eliminate missing-feedback or exposure bias.

Keep repeated candidate draws nested within users; they are not independent users. Report candidate-draw variability separately from user uncertainty. These intervals describe validation uncertainty conditional on the trained checkpoint, not training-seed variability or protection against repeated-search overfitting.

## Current Code Workflow (from code analyzer)
# Model Overview (for Diagnosis)

The supplied module diagnoses one fitted HSTU model per category. It accesses effective item embeddings through `item_emb`, causal sequence features through `log2feats(sequence)`, and aligned or candidate scores through `predict_score(features, items)`. Inputs contain item IDs and learned absolute positions. For left-padded histories, the final representation comes from the greatest nonpadding index, never `count-1`. Backbone implementation details are not supplied.

# Diagnosis Inputs & Hooks

`DiagnosisProbe(view, device)` receives the host ModelView; `view.model` is the actual network. It reads catalog size, maximum sequence length, category identity, and `user_train['History']`. Loader batches provide `(None, sequence, positive, negative)` with matching B × L tensors; shapes and item IDs are validated.

`run_full_diagnosis` caches at most ten batches, enables evaluation/inference mode, and restores module modes and captured random-generator states afterward.

# Probes & Metrics

- **Embedding collapse:** Samples up to 2,048 item embeddings and rescales their mean off-diagonal cosine to [0,1]. Approximately 0.5 means zero mean cosine; values near 1 indicate strong angular alignment. This does not measure representation rank or recommendation diversity.
- **Positive–negative margins:** Reports mean margin, tenth percentile, negative-wins rate, and fraction below 0.5 over valid training positions. Larger margins and fewer ranking errors generally indicate stronger sampled-pair separation; the threshold depends on score scale.
- **History audit:** Reports original rank, reciprocal rank, and hit@10, plus paired intervention effects. Lower rank and higher reciprocal rank/hit@10 indicate better target placement.
- **Cost:** Records wall time, CUDA interval, peak allocation, and scoring counts.

# Perturbation & Tests

Up to 32 training users contribute two prefixes each; loader rows provide a fallback. Each prefix shares one target and up to 999 unique negatives across variants. Tests remove recent, oldest, final, or prefinal events, and average three nonfinal shuffles. Deletions compact histories and restore left padding. Effects measure frozen-model sensitivity; user-cluster bootstrapping supplies conditional intervals when identities permit.

# MODEL_DIAGNOSIS Schema & Limitations

Output contains `metrics` and `metric_definitions`, including coverage, exclusions, effects, uncertainty, and null reasons. Unavailable category breakdowns and four-category macro estimates remain empty/null. These training diagnostics do not establish validation performance, generalization, intent, elapsed-time effects, diversity, or conformity.
